Saygin, D., Patel, M.K., Worrell, E., Tam, C. and Gielen, D.J. (2011). Potential of best practice technology to improve energy efficiency in the global chemical and petrochemical sector. Energy 36(9), 5779-5790. doi:10.1016/j.energy.2011.05.019. Based on the IEA Information Paper "Chemical and Petrochemical Sector: Potential of best practice technology and other measures for improving energy efficiency" (OECD/IEA 2009). Supplementary background document held as saygin_2011_chemical-best-practice-technology-si_energy.doc.

Locators are printed journal page numbers (5779-5790; PDF page = printed - 5778). Main file: Table 1 BPT and average current SEC (2006, mostly European data applied globally) for 56 of 57 processes (oxygen: electricity only, no value), loaded per carrier as fuel ("Heat" column) and steam; final energy, LHV, excluding electricity. Negative steam = net export; pdftotext drops the minus glyph, so signs were checked against the rendered table. Steam-cracking rows for benzene, butadiene and propylene repeat the ethylene values (13.1 / -1.4) and are loaded once as Ethylene; toluene, xylene, butylene and propylene (FCC) repeat the aromatics-extraction steam values (1.9 / 3.2) and are loaded once as Benzene (aromatics extraction). Ethane cracker fuel derived as 13.1+5 (footnote f). Table 2 average current SEC (fuel and steam combined, target blank) for Canada, USA and World in the main file; the other 11 countries in _other-values. Feedstock column (calorific value of product) in _other-values. Many values are author estimates (BPT = average less 20%, footnote c; average = BPT plus 20%, footnote b), flagged in the notes. The SI (mmc1.doc) holds only coverage-correction and uncertainty analysis, no technology data, so nothing was extracted from it. saygin_2012_001 (cited by UKERC for biomass boilers) does not appear to be this work, so a new id is used.
